source_text: Ὁ γνωστικὸς ἄρα τὴν προσεχεστέραν ἀναμάσσεται ὁμοιότητα, τὴν διάνοιαν τὴν τοῦ διδασκάλου, ἥντινα ἐκεῖνος νοῶν ἐνετείλατό τε καὶ συνεβούλευσε τοῖς φρονίμοις καὶ σώφροσι, ταύτην συνιείς, ὡς ὁ διδάξας ἐβούλετο, καὶ ἰδίᾳ τὴν νόησιν ἀναλαβὼν τὴν μεγαλοπρεπῆ, διδάξας μὲν ἀξιολόγως ἐπὶ τῶν δωμάτων τοὺς ὑψηλῶς οἰκοδομεῖσθαι δυναμένους, προκατάρξας δὲ τῆς τῶν λεγομένων ἐνεργείας κατὰ τὸ ὑπόδειγμα τῆς πολιτείας· δυνατὰ γὰρ ἐνετείλατο, καὶ δεῖ τῷ ὄντι ἀρχικὸν εἶναι καὶ ἡγεμονικὸν τὸν βασιλικόν τε καὶ Χριστιανόν, ἐπεὶ μὴ τῶν ἔξω μόνον θηρίων κατακυριεύειν ἐτάγημεν, ἀλλὰ καὶ τῶν ἐν ἡμῖν αὐτοῖς ἀγρίων παθῶν. κατ’ ἐπίστασιν οὖν, ὡς ἔοικεν, τοῦ κακοῦ καὶ ἀγαθοῦ βίου σῴζεται ὁ γνωστικός, πλέον τῶν γραμματέων καὶ Φαρισαίων συνιείς τε καὶ ἐνεργῶν.
pass_a_gloss: The gnostic therefore will chew the nearest likeness, the mind of the teacher, which that one, understanding, commanded and advised the prudent and self-controlled, this one understanding, as the one who taught wished, and having taken up privately the great-minded notion, having taught worthily those who are able to be built up highly on the roofs, but having begun beforehand the activity of the things being said according to the model of the polity; for he commanded powerful things, and it is necessary for the one who is to be archaic and hegemonic, the royal and Christian, since we were not ordered to rule only the external beasts, but also the wild passions in ourselves. Therefore, according to knowledge, as it seems, of the bad and good life, the gnostic is saved, more than the scribes and Pharisees, understanding and acting.
pass_b_english: The gnostic therefore chews over the closest likeness — the mind of the teacher. That teacher, after understanding it, both commanded and advised the prudent and self-controlled. The gnostic grasps this mind exactly as the one who taught intended. Taking up that noble concept privately, he teaches worthily those who can be built up to a high standard, and he begins the work of putting these words into practice according to the model of the polity. For the teacher commanded powerful things, and the person who is to be both foundational and authoritative — the royal and Christian figure — must truly exercise rule. We were appointed not only to master external beasts but also the wild passions within ourselves. Thus, by means of knowledge, as it appears, of the bad and good life, the gnostic is saved — surpassing the scribes and Pharisees in both understanding and action.

anf_compare.notes: Drafted from source only; ANF not shown to drafter.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the complex syntax of the Greek. Pass A and Pass B both correctly handle the 'gnostic' as the subject of the first clause. Pass B provides a more fluent rendering of the relative clauses and the 'archaic/hegemonic' section while remaining faithful to the Greek meaning. The term 'ἀναμάσσεται' is rendered as 'chew' (A) and 'chews over' (B), which is a literal and correct translation of the Greek verb.
